title: FloodGuard Renewal Conditions
content:
Renewal conditions of the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy: continuity of coverage, the renewal grace period, changes that wait for renewal, and nonrenewal for repetitive loss.

## 1. Continuity and the grace period

1.1 The renewal keeps coverage continuous only when the renewal premium is received no later than the renewal grace period that starts on the expiration date.

1.2 The renewal grace period is counted in calendar days from the expiration date, and payment on the last day is on time. The expiration date on the policy record is the start of the count, for that policy.

1.3 A renewal paid within the grace period takes effect on the expiring expiration date with no waiting period, for a new twelve-month term.

1.4 After the grace period the policy expires as of its expiration date, with renewal not paid as the reason, and new coverage needs a new application with a new waiting period.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, a 30-day grace period as on every FloodGuard tier).**

| Expiration date | Renewal premium received | On time? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 1 July (day 30, the last day) | Yes | Renewal effective 1 June, no waiting period |
| 1 June | 2 July (day 31) | No | Policy expires as of 1 June; a new application with a new waiting period is needed |

## 2. Changes that wait for renewal

Limit decreases and deductible changes the named insured asks for take effect only at renewal.

## 3. Nonrenewal for repetitive loss

3.1 The building is nonrenewed for repetitive loss when its count of repetitive losses reaches the tier's repetitive loss count on the renewal offer date.

3.2 The count is the number of distinct flood claims whose unvoided flood claim payments total more than the tier's smallest counted claim, within the tier's lookback years ending on the renewal offer date, across every flood policy that has insured the same property address.

3.3 Notice of the nonrenewal is given at least the tier's nonrenewal notice days before expiration to the named insured, and the tier's mortgagee notice days to the mortgagee. The policy then expires at its expiration date with repetitive loss as the reason.

**Hypothetical count.** On a tier with a count of 2, a smallest counted claim of 1,000 USD and a lookback of 10 years, an address shows, within the 10 years ending on the renewal offer date, claim A with payments of 3,000 USD, claim B with payments of 1,500 USD of which 700 USD was voided, and claim C, on an earlier FloodGuard policy at the same address, with payments of 2,200 USD. Claim B totals 800 USD unvoided and is not counted; claims A and C are counted. The count is 2, which reaches the tier's count, and the building is nonrenewed.
